text: DNA shuffling, developed by Stemmer in 1994, generates recombinant genes by which method?
choices: Fragmenting homologous parent genes with DNase I, then reassembling the fragments via primerless PCR relying on their sequence homology
Randomizing a single codon position using NNK degenerate primers
Treating cells with EMS to alkylate guanine bases genome-wide
Displaying protein variants on phage coat proteins for affinity panning
explanation: DNA shuffling fragments multiple homologous parent genes with DNase I and reassembles full-length recombinants via PCR without primers, relying on roughly 50% sequence homology between the fragments to prime each other, generating chimeric genes. NNK randomization instead describes saturation mutagenesis at a single position, EMS treatment is a chemical point-mutagenesis method unrelated to recombination, and phage display is a selection method for finding binders, not a diversity-generation or recombination technique.
